Chapter 8: The Ongoing Journey—Faith as a Daily Walk.
You know, a lot of people picture faith as this huge, mountaintop moment—one powerful experience that changes everything. But, truth is, for most of us, faith looks a lot more like a steady walk. It’s all those small steps, the little setbacks, the quiet moments when we keep trying, even if no one else sees it.
Let’s talk about what that really means. Instead of seeing faith as some far-off destination, what if you saw it as a journey—something that unfolds one day at a time?
Picture this: a retiree who’d spent decades working suddenly finds himself with all the time in the world, but none of the structure he was used to. He tried volunteering, picked up some hobbies, even reached out to old friends, but deep down, something still felt missing.
One morning, almost on a whim, he decides to start each day by sitting at the window, watching the sunrise, and offering a silent prayer of gratitude. At first, it’s awkward—maybe even a little pointless. But as the weeks go by, something shifts. The days don’t feel so empty. He starts to notice little opportunities for kindness and connection—things he used to overlook.
Here’s something to pay attention to: we tend to underestimate the power of small, steady habits. Our minds love big, dramatic changes, but our hearts? They’re shaped by what we choose to do every single day. Faith doesn’t grow through grand gestures. It grows in those quiet choices—to show up, to listen, to trust, and to love.
Now, let’s look at another example. There’s a teenager, wrestling with questions about who she is and where she belongs. She finds comfort in journaling—just writing down her fears, her hopes, her prayers before bed. Some nights, the words come easily. Other times, it’s a struggle just to get anything on the page. But night after night, that journal becomes a safe place—a companion where she can be honest, wrestle with her doubts, and hold onto hope.
Looking back, she realizes her faith didn’t grow because she found all the answers. It grew because she kept asking questions. She kept showing up, even on the hard days.
The journey of faith isn’t a straight line. There are seasons of doubt, moments of clarity, and times when the path ahead just isn’t clear. But every step—no matter how small—matters. The retiree keeps up his morning ritual and discovers new meaning in his days. The teenager, through her writing, finds a sense of belonging she never thought possible.
So, here’s the key takeaway: faith isn’t a one-time event. It’s a daily walk—a journey marked by presence, persistence, and the quiet courage to keep going, one step at a time.
